cues.en: Let's talk about space filling curves. They are incredibly fun to animate, and they also give a chance to address a certain philosophical question.
cues.zh: 我们来聊聊空间填充曲线。把它们做成动画非常有趣，而且这也给我们提供了一个探讨某种哲学问题的机会。

cues.en: Math often deals with infinite quantities, sometimes so intimately that the very substance of a result only actually makes sense in an infinite world.
cues.zh: 数学经常处理无限量的问题，有时这种结合如此紧密，以至于某个结果的真正实质只有在一个无限的世界中才有意义。

cues.en: So the question is, how can these results ever be useful in a finite context?
cues.zh: 所以问题是，这些结果怎么可能在有限的语境下派上用场呢？

cues.en: As with all philosophizing,
cues.zh: 跟所有的哲学思考一样，

cues.en: this is best left to discuss until after we look at the concrete case and the real math. So I'll begin by laying down an application of something called a Hilbert curve,
cues.zh: 最好等我们看过了具体案例和真正的数学之后再来讨论。所以我先介绍一下被称为希尔伯特曲线的应用，

cues.en: followed by a description of some of its origins in infinite math.
cues.zh: 接着再描述它在无限数学中的一些起源。

cues.en: Let's say that you wanted to write some software that would enable people to see with their ears.
cues.zh: 假设你想编写一些软件，让人能够用耳朵去“看见”。

cues.en: It would take in data from a camera and then somehow
cues.zh: 它会接收来自摄像头的数码，然后以某种有意义的方式

cues.en: translate that into a sound in a meaningful way.
cues.zh: 将其转化为声音。

cues.en: The thought here is that brains are plastic enough to build an intuition from sight even when the raw data is scrambled into a different format.
cues.zh: 这里的想法是，大脑具有足够的塑性，即使原始数据被混排成不同的格式，也能从中建立起视觉直觉。

cues.en: I've left a few links in the description to studies to this effect.
cues.zh: 我在简介里留了一些关于这方面研究的链接。

cues.en: To make initial experiments easier, you might start by treating incoming images with a low resolution, maybe 256
cues.zh: 为了让初步实验更简单，你可能会从处理低分辨率的输入图像开始，比如 256

cues.en: by 256 pixels.
cues.zh: 乘 256 像素。

cues.en: And to make my own animation efforts easier, let's represent one of these images with a square grid, each cell corresponding with a pixel.
cues.zh: 为了让我的动画制作更简单，我们用一个正方形网格来表示其中一幅图像，每个格子对应一个像素。

cues.en: One approach to this sound to sight software
cues.zh: 一种将声音转化为视觉的方法

cues.en: would be to find a nice way to associate each one of those pixels with a unique frequency value.
cues.zh: 是找到一种巧妙的方式，将每个像素与一个独特的频率值关联起来。

cues.en: Then when that pixel is brighter, the frequency associated with it would be played louder.
cues.zh: 这样，当像素更亮时，与之关联的频率就会播放得更响亮。

cues.en: And if the pixel were darker,
cues.zh: 而如果像素更暗，

cues.en: the frequency would be quiet.
cues.zh: 频率就会更轻。

cues.en: Listening to all of the pixels all at once would then sound like a bunch of frequencies overlaid on top of one another with dominant frequencies corresponding to the brighter regions of the image sounding like some cacophonous mess until your brain learns to make sense out of the information that it contains.
cues.zh: 同时聆听所有像素的声音，就像一堆频率叠加在一起，其中主导频率对应图像中较亮的区域，听起来像是一团嘈杂的混乱，直到你的大脑学会理解其中包含的信息。

cues.en: Let's temporarily set aside worries about whether or not this would actually work and instead think about what function from pixel space down to frequency space gives this software the best chance of working.
cues.zh: 让我们暂时放下这种方法是否真的有效的担忧，转而思考从像素空间到频率空间的哪种函数能给这个软件带来最大的成功机会。

cues.en: The tricky part is that pixel space is two dimensional,
cues.zh: 棘手之处在于像素空间是二维的，

cues.en: but frequency space is one dimensional.
cues.zh: 而频率空间是一维的。

cues.en: You could, of course, try doing this with a random mapping.
cues.zh: 当然，你可以尝试用随机映射来实现。

cues.en: After all, we're hoping that people's brains make sense out of pretty wonky data anyway.
cues.zh: 毕竟，我们希望人们的大脑无论如何都能理解相当古怪的数据。

cues.en: However, it might be nice to leverage some of the intuitions that a given human brain already has about sound.
cues.zh: 不过，利用人类大脑对声音已有的某些直觉可能会更好。

cues.en: For example, if we think in terms of the reverse mapping from frequency space to pixel space,
cues.zh: 例如，如果我们从频率空间到像素空间的逆向映射来思考，

cues.en: frequencies that are close together
cues.zh: 相近的频率

cues.en: should stay close together in the pixel space.
cues.zh: 在像素空间中应该保持接近。

cues.en: That way, even if an ear has a hard time distinguishing between two nearby frequencies,
cues.zh: 那样的话，即使耳朵很难分辨两个相近的频率，

cues.en: they will at least refer to the same basic point in space.
cues.zh: 它们至少会指向空间中同一个基本点。

cues.en: To ensure that this happens, you could first describe a way to weave a line through each one of these pixels.
cues.zh: 为确保做到这一点，你可以先描述一种方法，让一条线穿过这些像素中的每一个。

cues.en: Then if you fix each pixel to a spot on that line and
cues.zh: 然后，如果把每个像素固定到那条线上的某个位置，

cues.en: unravel the whole thread to make it straight,
cues.zh: 再把整条线展开拉直，

cues.en: you could interpret this line as a frequency space,
cues.zh: 你就可以把这条线看成一个频率空间，

cues.en: and you have an association
cues.zh: 这样你就有了一个关联

cues.en: from pixels to frequencies,
cues.zh: 从像素到频率的关联，

cues.en: which is what we want.
cues.zh: 这正是我们想要的。

cues.en: Now one weaving method would be to just go one row at a time, alternating between left and right as it moves up that pixel space.
cues.zh: 一种编织方法是每次只走一行，在像素空间中向上移动时左右交替。

cues.en: This is like a well played game of snake, so let's call this a snake curve.
cues.zh: 这就像一局玩得很顺的贪吃蛇游戏，所以我们把它叫作蛇形曲线。

cues.en: When you tell your mathematician friend about this idea, she says, why not use a Hilbert curve?
cues.zh: 当你把这个想法告诉你的数学家朋友时，她说，为什么不用希尔伯特曲线？

cues.en: When you ask her what that is, she stumbles for a moment.
cues.zh: 你问她那是什么，她一时语塞。

cues.en: So it's not a curve, but an infinite family of curves, she starts.
cues.zh: “所以它不是一条曲线，而是一个无限的曲线族，”她开始说。

cues.en: Well, no. It actually is just one thing, but I need to tell you about a certain infinite family first.
cues.zh: “呃，不。它其实只是一个东西，但我得先给你讲某个无限的曲线族。”

cues.en: She pulls out a piece of paper and starts explaining what she decides to call pseudo Hilbert curves, for lack of a better term.
cues.zh: 她拿出一张纸，开始解释她决定称作伪希尔伯特曲线的东西，因为一时想不到更好的说法。

cues.en: For an order one pseudo Hilbert curve,
cues.zh: 对于一阶伪希尔伯特曲线，

cues.en: you divide a square into a two by two grid and connect the center of the lower left quadrant
cues.zh: 你把一个正方形分成 2×2 的网格，然后连接左下象限的中心

cues.en: to the center of the upper left
cues.zh: 到左上象限的中心

cues.en: over to the upper right and then down in the lower right.
cues.zh: 再到右上，然后向下到右下。

cues.en: For an order two pseudo Hilbert curve,
cues.zh: 对于二阶伪希尔伯特曲线，

cues.en: rather than just going straight from one quadrant to another, we let our curve do a little work to fill out each quadrant while it does so.
cues.zh: 我们不只是直接从一个象限走到另一个象限，而是让曲线在穿过时做点额外的工作来填满每个象限。

cues.en: Specifically,
cues.zh: 具体来说，

cues.en: subdivide the square further into a four by four grid, and we have our curve trace out a miniature order one pseudo Hilbert curve inside each quadrant before it moves on to the next.
cues.zh: 把正方形进一步细分为 4x4 的网格，在移动到下一个象限之前，让曲线在每个象限内部追踪一条迷你的一阶伪希尔伯特曲线。

cues.en: If we left those mini curves oriented as they are, going from the end of the mini curve in the lower left to the start of the mini curve in the upper left requires this kind of awkward jump. Same deal with going from the upper right down to the lower right.
cues.zh: 如果我们让这些迷你曲线保持原来的方向，从左下角迷你曲线的终点走到左上角迷你曲线的起点，就会需要这种尴尬的跳跃。从右上角到右下角的情况也一样。

cues.en: So we flip the curves in the lower left and the lower right to make that connection shorter.
cues.zh: 所以我们把左下和右下的曲线翻转一下，让连接变得更短。

cues.en: Going from an order two to an order three pseudo Hilbert curve is completely similar. You divide the square into an eight by eight grid,
cues.zh: 从二阶到三阶伪希尔伯特曲线完全是类似的。你把正方形划分为 8x8 的网格，

cues.en: then you put an order two pseudo Hilbert curve in each quadrant,
cues.zh: 然后在每个象限放入一条二阶伪希尔伯特曲线，

cues.en: flip the lower left and the lower right ones appropriately,
cues.zh: 适当地翻转左下和右下的曲线，

cues.en: and then connect them all tip to tail.
cues.zh: 然后把它们首尾相连。

cues.en: And the pattern continues like that for higher orders.
cues.zh: 对于更高阶数，这个规律也是一样的。

cues.en: For the 256
cues.zh: 对于 256

cues.en: by 256
cues.zh: 乘以 256

cues.en: pixel array, your mathematician friend explains,
cues.zh: 的像素数组，你的数学家朋友解释说，

cues.en: you would use an order eight pseudo Hilbert curve.
cues.zh: 你会使用一条八阶伪希尔伯特曲线。

cues.en: And remember, defining a curve which weaves through each pixel is basically the same as defining a function from pixel space to frequency space since you're associating each pixel with a point on the line.
cues.zh: 记住，定义一条穿过每个像素的曲线，基本上就等于定义了一个从像素空间到频率空间的函数，因为你是把每个像素与线上的一个点关联起来。

cues.en: Now, this is nice as a piece of art, but why would these pseudo Hilbert curves be any better than just the snake curve?
cues.zh: 作为一件艺术品，这很不错，但为什么这些伪希尔伯特曲线会比简单的蛇形曲线更好呢？

cues.en: Well, here's one very important reason.
cues.zh: 嗯，这里有一个非常重要的原因。

cues.en: Imagine that you go through with this project, you integrate the software with real cameras and headphones, and it works. People around the world are using the device, building intuitions for vision via sound.
cues.zh: 想象一下，你完成了这个项目，将软件与真实的摄像头和耳机集成，并且它运行良好。全世界的人们都在使用这个设备，通过声音建立对视觉的直觉。

cues.en: What happens when you issue an upgrade that increases the resolution of the camera's image from two fifty six by two fifty six to five twelve by five twelve?
cues.zh: 当你发布一个升级，将摄像头图像的分辨率从256乘256提高到512乘512时，会发生什么？

cues.en: If you were using the snake curve,
cues.zh: 如果你使用的是蛇形曲线，

cues.en: as you transition to a higher resolution,
cues.zh: 当你过渡到更高分辨率时，

cues.en: many points on this frequency line would have to go to completely different parts of pixel space.
cues.zh: 这条频率线上的许多点将不得不移动到像素空间中完全不同的位置。

cues.en: For example, let's follow a point about halfway along the frequency line.
cues.zh: 例如，让我们沿着频率线大约一半位置的一个点来看。

cues.en: It'll end up about halfway up the pixel space no matter the resolution,
cues.zh: 无论分辨率如何，它最终都会位于像素空间大约一半高度的位置，

cues.en: but where it is left to right can differ wildly
cues.zh: 但它左右的位置可能会大相径庭，

cues.en: as you go from two fifty six up to five twelve.
cues.zh: 当你从256升级到512时。

cues.en: This means everyone using your software would have to relearn how to see with their ears since the original intuitions of which points in space correspond to which frequencies
cues.zh: 这意味着所有使用你软件的人都必须重新学习如何用耳朵看，因为原本关于空间中哪些点对应哪些频率的直觉

cues.en: no longer apply.
cues.zh: 不再适用了。

cues.en: However,
cues.zh: 然而，

cues.en: with the Hilbert curve technique,
cues.zh: 使用希尔伯特曲线技术，

cues.en: as you increase the order of a pseudo Hilbert curve, a given point on the line moves around less and less.
cues.zh: 当你提高伪希尔伯特曲线的阶数时，线上给定点的移动越来越少。

cues.en: It just approaches a more specific point in space.
cues.zh: 它只是趋近于空间中一个更具体的位置。

cues.en: That way, you've given your users the opportunity to fine tune their intuitions
cues.zh: 这样，你就让用户有机会微调自己的直觉

cues.en: rather than relearning everything.
cues.zh: 而不是重新学习一切。

cues.en: So for this sound to sight application,
cues.zh: 所以对于这个声音转图像的应用，

cues.en: the Hilbert curve approach turns out to be exactly what you want.
cues.zh: 希尔伯特曲线方法恰好就是你要的。

cues.en: In fact, given how specific the goal is,
cues.zh: 事实上，考虑到目标如此具体，

cues.en: it seems almost weirdly perfect.
cues.zh: 它几乎完美得有点奇怪。

cues.en: So you go back to your mathematician friend and you ask her, hey, what was the original motivation for defining one of these curves?
cues.zh: 于是你回去找你的数学家朋友，问她：嘿，定义这类曲线最初的动机是什么？

cues.en: She explains that near the end of the nineteenth century, in the aftershock of Cantor's research on infinity,
cues.zh: 她解释说，十九世纪末，在康托尔关于无穷的研究余波中，

cues.en: mathematicians were interested in finding a mapping from a one dimensional line into two dimensional space
cues.zh: 数学家们想找到一种从一维直线到二维空间的映射

cues.en: in such a way that the line runs through every single point in space.
cues.zh: 使得这条直线穿过空间中的每一个点。

cues.en: To be clear, we're not talking about a finite bounded grid of pixels like we had in the sound to sight application.
cues.zh: 需要说明的是，我们说的不是声音转图像应用里那种有限边界的像素网格。

cues.en: This is continuous space,
cues.zh: 这是连续空间，

cues.en: which is very infinite.
cues.zh: 无限得很。

cues.en: And the goal is to have a line, which is as thin as thin can be and has zero area,
cues.zh: 目标是让一条细得不能再细、面积为零的线，

cues.en: somehow pass through every single one of those infinitely many points that makes up the infinite area of space.
cues.zh: 设法穿过构成无限空间区域的每一个点，而这些点有无穷多个。

cues.en: Before 1890,
cues.zh: 在1890年之前，

cues.en: a lot of people thought that this was obviously impossible.
cues.zh: 很多人认为这显然是不可能的。

cues.en: But then Peano discovered the first of what would come to be known as space filling curves.
cues.zh: 但后来皮亚诺发现了后来被称为空间填充曲线的第一类曲线。

cues.en: Hilbert followed with his own slightly simpler space filling curve.
cues.zh: 希尔伯特随后提出了自己稍简单一些的空间填充曲线。

cues.en: Technically,
cues.zh: 严格来说，

cues.en: each one fills a square, not all of space, but I'll show you later on how once you filled a square with a line, filling all of space is not an issue.
cues.zh: 每条曲线填充的是一个正方形，而不是整个空间；但后面我会展示，一旦能用线填满一个正方形，填满整个空间就不成问题。

cues.en: By the way, mathematicians use this word curve to talk about a line running through space even if it has jagged corners.
cues.zh: 顺便说一句，数学家使用“曲线”这个词来讨论一条穿过空间的线，即使它有锯齿状的拐角。

cues.en: This is especially counterintuitive terminology in the context of a space filling curve, which in a sense consists of nothing but sharp corners.
cues.zh: 在空间填充曲线的语境下，这个术语尤其反直觉，因为从某种意义上说，它完全由尖锐的拐角组成。

cues.en: A better name might be something like space filling fractal, which some people do use,
cues.zh: 更好的名字可能是空间填充分形之类，有些人确实这么用，

cues.en: but hey, it's math, so we live with bad terminology.
cues.zh: 但嘿，这是数学，所以我们就忍受糟糕的术语吧。

cues.en: None of the pseudo Hilbert curves that you use to fill pixelated space would count as a space filling curve, no matter how high the order.
cues.zh: 你用来填充像素化空间的任何伪希尔伯特曲线，无论阶数多高，都不算作空间填充曲线。

cues.en: Just zoom in on one of the pixels.
cues.zh: 只需放大其中一个像素。

cues.en: When this pixel is considered part of infinite continuous
cues.zh: 当这个像素被视为无限连续

cues.en: space,
cues.zh: 空间的一部分时，

cues.en: the curve only passes through the tiniest zero area slice of it, and it certainly doesn't hit every single point.
cues.zh: 曲线只穿过它最微小的零面积切片，而且它当然不会触及每一个点。

cues.en: Your mathematician friend explains that an actual bona fide Hilbert curve is not any one of these pseudo Hilbert curves.
cues.zh: 你的数学家朋友解释说，真正的希尔伯特曲线不是这些伪希尔伯特曲线中的任何一条。

cues.en: Instead, it's the limit of all of them.
cues.zh: 相反，它是所有这些曲线的极限。

cues.en: Now defining this limit rigorously
cues.zh: 现在严格定义这个极限

cues.en: is delicate.
cues.zh: 是很微妙的。

cues.en: You first have to formalize what these curves are as functions.
cues.zh: 你首先必须将这些曲线形式化为函数。

cues.en: Specifically, functions which take in a single number somewhere between zero and one as their input
cues.zh: 具体来说，是以零到一之间的单个数字作为输入的函数

cues.en: and output a pair of numbers.
cues.zh: 并输出一对数字。

cues.en: This input can be thought of as a point on the line, and the output can be thought of as coordinates in two d space.
cues.zh: 这个输入可以看作直线上的一个点，输出可以看作二维空间中的坐标。

cues.en: But in principle, it's just an association between a single number and pairs of numbers.
cues.zh: 但原则上，它只是单个数字与数字对之间的关联。

cues.en: For example, an order two pseudo Hilbert curve as a function maps the input 0.3
cues.zh: 例如，作为一个函数的二阶伪希尔伯特曲线将输入 0.3

cues.en: to the output pair 0.125,
cues.zh: 映射到输出对 0.125，

cues.en: An order three pseudo Hilbert curve maps that same input 0.3
cues.zh: 三阶伪希尔伯特曲线将同样的输入 0.3

cues.en: to the output pair zero point zero seven five eight zero point six eight seven five.
Now the core property that makes a function like this a curve and not just any old association between single numbers and pairs of numbers is continuity.
cues.zh: 现在，使这样一个函数成为一条曲线，而不仅仅是单数和数对之间任意关联的核心属性，是连续性。

cues.en: The intuition behind continuity
cues.zh: 连续性背后的直觉

cues.en: is that you don't want the output of your function to suddenly jump at any point when the input is only changing smoothly.
cues.zh: 是当输入仅在平滑变化时，你不希望函数的输出在任何点突然发生跳跃。

cues.en: And the way that this is made rigorous in math is... Well, it's actually pretty clever, and fully appreciating space filling curves really does require digesting the formal idea of continuity.
cues.zh: 而在数学中使其严谨的方法是……嗯，其实相当巧妙，要真正理解空间填充曲线确实需要消化连续性的形式化概念。

cues.en: So it's definitely worth taking a brief sidestep to go over it now.
cues.zh: 所以现在花点时间稍微绕道复习一下绝对是值得的。

cues.en: Consider a particular input point, a, and the corresponding output of the function, b.
cues.zh: 考虑一个特定的输入点 a，以及函数对应的输出 b。

cues.en: Draw a circle centered around a and look at all of the other input points inside that circle, and then consider where the function takes all of those points in the output space.
cues.zh: 画一个以 a 为中心的圆，看看该圆内的所有其他输入点，然后考虑函数将所有这些点映射到输出空间中的什么位置。

cues.en: Now draw the smallest circle that you can centered at b that contains those outputs.
cues.zh: 现在以 b 为中心，画一个包含这些输出的最小的圆。

cues.en: Different choices for the size of the input circle might result in larger or smaller circles in the output space.
cues.zh: 输入圆大小的不同选择可能会导致输出空间中更大或更小的圆。

cues.en: But notice what happens when we go through this process at a point where the function jumps.
cues.zh: 但请注意，当我们在函数发生跳跃的点上经历这个过程时会发生什么。

cues.en: Drawing a circle around a and looking at the input points within the circle,
cues.zh: 以 a 为圆心画一个圆，观察圆内的输入点，

cues.en: seeing where they map,
cues.zh: 看它们映射到哪里，

cues.en: and drawing the smallest possible circle centered at b containing those points.
cues.zh: 再以 b 为圆心，画一个包含这些点的尽可能小的圆。

cues.en: No matter how small the circle around a,
cues.zh: 无论 a 周围的圆多小，

cues.en: the corresponding circle around b just cannot be smaller than that jump.
cues.zh: b 周围对应的圆都不可能小于这个跳跃幅度。

cues.en: For this reason, we say that the function is discontinuous
cues.zh: 因此，我们说该函数在 a 处不连续——

cues.en: at a if there's any lower bound on the size of this circle that surrounds b.
cues.zh: 只要 b 周围这个圆的大小存在任何下界。

cues.en: If on the other hand, the circle around b can be made as small as you want with sufficiently small choices for circles around a, you say that the function is continuous at a.
cues.zh: 反过来，如果 a 周围的圆取得足够小，就能让 b 周围的圆任意小，那么就说该函数在 a 处连续。

cues.en: A function as a whole is called continuous if it's continuous at every possible input point.
cues.zh: 如果一个函数在每个可能的输入点都连续，就称它整体是连续的。

cues.en: Now with that as a formal definition of curves,
cues.zh: 有了这个曲线的形式化定义，

cues.en: you're ready to define what an actual Hilbert curve is.
cues.zh: 你就可以定义真正的 Hilbert 曲线了。

cues.en: Doing this relies on a wonderful property of the sequence of pseudo Hilbert curves, which should feel familiar.
cues.zh: 这依赖于伪 Hilbert 曲线序列的一个绝妙性质，你应该会觉得似曾相识。

cues.en: Take a given input point, like 0.3,
cues.zh: 取一个给定的输入点，比如 0.3，

cues.en: and apply each successive pseudo Hilbert curve function to this point.
cues.zh: 对它依次应用每一个伪 Hilbert 曲线函数。

cues.en: The corresponding outputs, as we increase the order of the curve,
cues.zh: 随着曲线阶数增加，对应的输出

cues.en: approaches some particular point in space.
cues.zh: 会趋近于空间中的某个特定点。

cues.en: It doesn't matter what input you start with. This sequence of outputs you get by applying each successive pseudo Hilbert curve to this point always stabilizes
cues.zh: 无论你从哪个输入开始，依次对这点应用每一个伪 Hilbert 曲线得到的输出序列总会稳定下来，

cues.en: and approaches some particular point in two d space.
cues.zh: 趋近于二维空间中的某个特定点。

cues.en: This is absolutely not true by the way for snake curves or for that matter most sequences of curves filling pixelated space of higher and higher resolutions.
cues.zh: 顺便说一句，对于蛇形曲线，或者说对于大多数填充更高、更高分辨率像素化空间的曲线序列来说，这绝对不是真的。

cues.en: The outputs associated with a given input become wildly erratic as the resolution increases,
cues.zh: 随着分辨率的提高，与给定输入关联的输出会变得极其不稳定，

cues.en: always jumping from left to right and never actually approaching anything.
cues.zh: 总是在左右跳跃，实际上永远不会接近任何东西。

cues.en: Now because of this property,
cues.zh: 现在，由于这个特性，

cues.en: we can define a Hilbert curve function like this.
cues.zh: 我们可以这样定义一个希尔伯特曲线函数。

cues.en: For a given input value between zero and one, consider the sequence of points in two d space you get by applying each successive pseudo Hilbert curve function at that point.
cues.zh: 对于零到一之间的给定输入值，考虑在那个点应用每个连续的伪希尔伯特曲线函数所得到的二维空间中的点序列。

cues.en: The output of the Hilbert curve function evaluated on this input is just defined to be the limit of those points.
cues.zh: 在此外输入上评估的希尔伯特曲线函数的输出，就被定义为这些点的极限。

cues.en: Because the sequence of pseudo Hilbert curve outputs always converges no matter what input you start with, this is actually a well defined function in a way that it never could have been had we used snake curves.
cues.zh: 因为无论你从什么输入开始，伪希尔伯特曲线输出的序列总是收敛的，所以这实际上是一个定义良好的函数，而如果我们使用蛇形曲线，这是永远不可能做到的。

cues.en: Now I'm not gonna go through the proof for why this gives a space filling curve, but let's at least see what needs to be proved.
cues.zh: 现在我不会去讲为什么这会产生一个空间填充曲线的证明，但让我们至少看看需要证明什么。

cues.en: First, verify that this is a well defined function by proving that the outputs of the pseudo Hilbert curve functions really do converge the way that I'm telling you they do.
cues.zh: 首先，通过证明伪希尔伯特曲线函数的输出确实如我所说的那样收敛，来验证这是一个定义良好的函数。

cues.en: Second, show that this function gives a curve,
cues.zh: 其次，证明这个函数产生了一条曲线，

cues.en: meaning it's continuous.
cues.zh: 这意味着它是连续的。

cues.en: Third and most important, show that it fills space in the sense that every single point in the unit square is an output of this function.
cues.zh: 第三也是最重要的一点，证明它确实填充了空间，即单位正方形中的每一个点都是该函数的输出。

cues.en: I really do encourage anyone watching this to take a stab at each one of these.
cues.zh: 我真的非常鼓励正在看视频的各位，亲自动手尝试一下这当中的每一个。

cues.en: Spoiler alert, all three of these facts turn out to be true.
cues.zh: 剧透一下，这三个事实最终全都是真的。

cues.en: You can extend this to a curve that fills all of space just by tiling space with squares and then chaining a bunch of Hilbert curves together in a spiraling pattern of tiles,
cues.zh: 你可以把这个方法推广到一条填满整个空间的曲线，只需用正方形铺满空间，然后把一堆希尔伯特曲线按螺旋形的区块图案串联起来，

cues.en: connecting the end of one tile to the start of a new tile with an added little stretch of line if you need to.
cues.zh: 如果需要的话，还可以用一小段延伸的直线，把一个区块的终点和下一个区块的起点连起来。

cues.en: You can think of the first tile as coming from the interval from zero to one, the second tile as coming from the interval from one to two, and so on.
cues.zh: 你可以把第一个区块想象成对应从 0 到 1 的区间，第二个区块对应从 1 到 2 的区间，以此类推。

cues.en: So the entire positive real number line is getting mapped into all of two d space.
cues.zh: 于是，整条正实数数轴就被映射到了整个二维空间中。

cues.en: Take a moment to let that fact sink in. A line, the platonic form of thinness itself,
cues.zh: 花点时间消化一下这个事实：一条线，这个纯粹“纤细”本身的柏拉图式形态，

cues.en: can wander through an infinitely extending and richly dense space and hit every single point.
cues.zh: 竟然能够在一个无限延伸且无限稠密的空间中穿行，并击中每一个点。

cues.en: Notice the core property that made pseudo Hilbert curves useful in both the sound to sight application
cues.zh: 请注意，使得伪希尔伯特曲线在“声转图”应用中

cues.en: and in their infinite origins
cues.zh: 以及在其无限延伸的源头中都大显身手的核心特性，

cues.en: is that points on the curve move around less and less as you increase the order of those curves.
cues.zh: 就是随着你提高这些曲线的阶数，曲线上的点移动得越来越少。

cues.en: While translating images to sound, this was useful because it means upgrading to higher resolutions
cues.zh: 在将图像转化为声音时，这一点非常有用，因为这意味着升级到更高的分辨率

cues.en: doesn't require retraining your senses all over again.
cues.zh: 并不需要你重新去训练自己的感官。

cues.en: For mathematicians
cues.zh: 对于那些

cues.en: interested in filling continuous space,
cues.zh: 对填满连续空间感兴趣的数学家来说，

cues.en: this property is what ensured that talking about the limit of a sequence of curves was actually a meaningful thing to do.
cues.zh: 正是这个特性，确保了探讨曲线序列的极限是一件切实有意义的事情。

cues.en: And this connection here between the infinite and the finite worlds seems to be more of a rule in math than an exception.
cues.zh: 而这里无限世界与有限世界之间的联系，在数学中似乎更像是一条规律，而不是特例。

cues.en: Another example that several astute commenters on the inventing math video pointed out is the connection between the divergent sum of all powers of two and the way that the number negative one is represented in computers with bits.
cues.zh: 另一个例子是，“发明数学”视频的几位精明评论者指出的：所有 2 的幂的发散求和，与计算机中用比特表示负一的方式之间的联系。

cues.en: It's not so much that the infinite result is directly useful,
cues.zh: 倒不是说这个无限的结果有多么直接的用处，

cues.en: but instead the same patterns and constructs that are used to define and prove infinite facts have finite analogs,
cues.zh: 而是因为那些用于定义和证明无限事实的相同模式和结构，拥有对应的有限形式，

cues.en: and these finite analogs are directly useful.
cues.zh: 并且这些有限形式是直接派上用场的。

cues.en: But the connection is often deeper than a mere analogy.
cues.zh: 但这种联系往往比单纯的类比更深。

cues.en: Many theorems about an infinite object are often equivalent to some theorem regarding a family of finite objects.
cues.zh: 许多关于无限对象的定理，通常等价于关于一族有限对象的某种定理。

cues.en: For example, if during your sound to sight project, you were to sit down and really formalize what it means for your curve to stay stable as you increase camera resolution,
cues.zh: 举个例子，如果在你的“声音转视觉”项目中，你坐下来认真形式化地定义：当增加相机分辨率时，曲线保持稳定究竟意味着什么，

cues.en: you would end up effectively writing the definition of what it means for a sequence of curves to have a limit.
cues.zh: 你最终实际上就会写出这样的定义：曲线序列拥有极限到底意味着什么。

cues.en: In fact, a statement about some infinite object, whether that's a sequence or a fractal,
cues.zh: 事实上，关于某个无限对象的陈述，无论是序列还是分形，

cues.en: can usually be viewed as a particularly clean way to encapsulate
cues.zh: 通常都可以被看作是一种特别简洁的方式，用来概括

cues.en: a truth about a family of finite objects.
cues.zh: 关于一族有限对象的真理。

cues.en: The lesson to take away here is that even when a statement seems very far removed from reality,
cues.zh: 这里我们要汲取的经验是，即便某个陈述看起来与现实相去甚远，

cues.en: you should always be willing to look under the hood and at the nuts and bolts of what's really being said.
cues.zh: 你也应该始终愿意去深入底层，探究其真正所表达的技术细节。

cues.en: Who knows? You might find insights for representing numbers from divergent sums or for seeing with your ears from filling space.
cues.zh: 谁知道呢？你也许能从发散和中获得表示数字的洞见，或从填充空间中获得用耳朵“看”的洞见。
